name: Aorto-left ventricular tunnel

criteria.description: Echocardiographic or imaging evidence of an abnormal tunnel-like communication between the ascending aorta and the left ventricle
Presence of aortic valve that is structurally normal or mildly affected without other intracardiac shunts
Signs of congestive heart failure or cardiac murmur in infancy or early childhood

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Visualization of the tunnel connecting the ascending aorta to the left ventricle on imaging plus exclusion of other intracardiac shunts
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily based on echocardiography and confirmed by cardiac MRI or catheterization if needed.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Continuous cardiac murmur with systolic and diastolic components
Echocardiographic evidence of aorto-left ventricular tunnel
searchTerms: heart ultrasound showing aorto-left ventricle tunnel
abnormal heart channel between aorta and left ventricle

common.symptomName: Congestive heart failure symptoms in infancy (tachypnea, feeding difficulties)
common.notes: Often presents within the first few months of life
searchTerms: breathing fast and feeding trouble in baby
congestive heart failure symptoms in infants
excess blood volume in left ventricle

rare.notes: Rare but reported in untreated cases

laboratory: Elevated brain natriuretic peptide (BNP) in heart failure
Normal inflammatory markers unless endocarditis present
imaging: Echocardiography showing tunnel communication from ascending aorta to left ventricle
Cardiac MRI or CT angiography confirming tunnel anatomy
genetic: No well-established genetic mutations identified; sporadic cases
other: Electrocardiogram may show left ventricular hypertrophy

distinguishingFeatures: Absence of tunnel communication on imaging
Shunt located at ventricular septum rather than aortic root
Abnormal communication between coronary artery and cardiac chamber
Different origin and course on imaging

redFlags: Rapid onset congestive heart failure in neonate
Continuous murmur with signs of volume overload
Sudden cardiac arrest or unexplained syncope
references: Mavroudis C, Backer CL. Aorto-left ventricular tunnel: surgical management and outcomes. Ann Thorac Surg. 2010.
Gatzoulis MA, et al. Diagnosis and management of congenital heart disease. Heart. 2017.
